grade_reason: Seven web searches and a review of his official press releases (November 2025 to October 2026) found no statement by Mrvan about AI at all, let alone about catastrophic risk.
notes: All seven web searches ran (six required plus one on Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act cosponsors); none was refused. The only AI-related hits were items reposted on mrvan.house.gov: a 31 July 2026 article on his visit to Purdue University Northwest's CIVS (https://mrvan.house.gov/media/in-the-news/us-rep-frank-j-mrvan-visits-pnw-civs-review-research-impacts), where AI appears only in the reporter's description of the research, not in Mrvan's quoted words (opened and checked); an earlier CIVS tour article (search summary says February; year not checked) and Daifuku plant articles where AI is mentioned by staff or the company CEO, not by Mrvan (not opened). Searches on superintelligence, extinction, pause or moratorium, China agreement and AI safety returned nothing about him; the moratorium search returned Rep. Frank Pallone, a different member. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (H.R. 10538, introduced by Casar 24 September 2026): no source lists Mrvan as a cosponsor, but no complete cosponsor list could be opened (congress.gov returned 403; QuiverQuant and Forkast name at most a few of the roughly 9 to 10 cosponsors), so his co-sponsorship is unconfirmed rather than ruled out. From the earlier attempt (still valid): mrvan.house.gov home page and press release listing pages (https://mrvan.house.gov/media/press-releases, ?page=1 to ?page=4, covering 24 November 2025 to 2 October 2026) had no title or visible excerpt mentioning AI, data centers or superintelligence (several excerpts truncated); the Utility Affordability and Transparency Act release (2 October 2026), the DOE utility affordability letter (22 June 2026) and the Energy Secretary hearing release (15 April 2026) do not mention AI or data centers. The site's search page returned 403. Press releases from January to November 2025 were not reviewed individually. Hearing transcripts and floor speeches were not searched beyond the web searches above.
